action.question: How should the main high-level overview be structured in the repo?

questions.question: How should the main high-level overview be structured in the repo?

options.label: Rewrite README as the overview
options.description: Make README.md the portfolio landing page (pitch + architecture + all systems + links). Move the current operational README content into docs/ as a deep technical reference. Nothing is lost; the front page becomes the overview. Best for a GitHub portfolio export.

options.label: New OVERVIEW.md, keep README
options.description: Add a separate OVERVIEW.md as the high-level pitch and leave the current detailed README untouched. Two top-level docs; README stays the operational manual.

options.label: Rewrite README + add ARCHITECTURE.md
options.description: README becomes the pitch/overview, plus a dedicated docs/ARCHITECTURE.md with diagrams and the deeper system-by-system technical breakdown. Most thorough split.

questions.question: Since this is for a portfolio export, how candid should the new overview be about your private infra?

options.label: Sanitized overview
options.description: Keep the new overview generic for an outside reader: 'two Macs', no internal IPs/NAS hostnames/home paths/GitHub username. Existing docs (DECISIONS.md etc.) stay as-is; only what I write is kept clean. Safer if it ever goes public.

options.label: Keep it candid
options.description: Write the overview with the real specifics (hostnames, paths, username) like the rest of the repo. More concrete, but exposes private infra details if published.
